business_problem: Impel's product and engineering teams were shipping new automotive AI capabilities faster than 150-plus customer-facing reps could learn them, while monthly business reviews and strategic projects still consumed hours of manual prep.
solution_summary: Impel uses Claude as the reasoning layer behind a portfolio of internal agents selected by business impact. For the highest-priority training problem, Claude analyzed more than 150,000 Gong calls plus Salesforce data to create a dealer roleplay agent that simulates hard conversations, speaks through speech-to-text and text-to-speech, and scores objection handling, rapport, product knowledge, and next steps before DMing scorecards in Slack. The company routes reasoning-heavy design work to Opus 4.5 and Fable 5.1 across MCP-connected workflows, then tests lighter Sonnet models as executor agents once a flow is proven. Beyond training, Snowflake-backed briefs reduce monthly business-review prep, and 400-plus Claude Enterprise seats extend the same agentic patterns into support, migrations, and knowledge work. This lets Impel treat agent building as an investment portfolio rather than a one-off experiment.

data_flow: Recorded Gong calls, Salesforce records, and Snowflake business data feed Claude-powered agent workflows; Fable or Opus reason over the hard parts, Sonnet executes stabilized tasks, and outputs such as roleplay scorecards or review briefs are delivered back to teams in Slack and other internal workflows.
business_outcome: Impel cut new-product ramp time from three to six months to about one month, reduced dealer business-review prep by roughly 85 percent, increased support-case throughput by 20 percent, and built its flagship roleplay agent in about three weeks while scaling Claude to more than 400 internal users.
